newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TASMANIA ROUT SOUTH AUSTRALIA BY 10 WICKETS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TASMANIA ROUT SOUTH AUSTRALIA BY 10 WICKETS.

text.p: All-rounder Shaun Young on Monday tore through a brittle South Australia batting line-up to hand Tasmania an emphatic 10-wicket victory over defending Sheffield Shield champions South Australia.
Seam bowler Young took four wickets in 25 balls as South Australia collapsed from their overnight score of 127 for six in their second innings to be all out for 142 at the Adelaide Oval.
Tasmania led by 132 runs on the first innings and openers Dene Hills and Jamie Cox safely brought up the required 11 runs for victory without loss.
Young first had middle-order batsman Geoff Parker caught by former Australia player David Boon at second slip after adding just three runs to his overnight score of 34.
South Australia meekly surrendered after the dismissal of Parker, the top-scorer of the innings, with Young removing the final three batsman for the addition of just one run.

The loss means South Australia, with three games remaining, are almost certain to finish last in this year's Shield standings. Tasmania leap-frogged Victoria into fourth place in the first-class competition between the six Australian states.
